hero.title: Escola Museo da Emigración
hero.lead: Preserving and sharing the historical memory and the creations of successive generations of emigrants.

gaxate.title: A story close to home, repeated all over Galicia
gaxate.text: The municipality of A Lama, and the parish of Gaxate in particular, are a striking example of a story close to home that repeats itself all over Galicia: the emigration of many young people who set out to seek their fortune while escaping hunger and compulsory military service.
gaxate.fact: An area where the vast majority of the population emigrated to the Americas in the early 20th century, and where many of the buildings are indiano houses.

escuela.title: A school built from the Americas
escuela.text: The Castro de Gaxate school was built in 1934 with money provided by Wenceslao Barreiro, a Gaxate local who worked as a rubber tapper in the Amazon, and with the labour of the villagers.
escuela.foot: Today, that same school is set to become the museum's home.

porque.quoteBefore: Despite the importance this phenomenon has had in our society,
porque.quoteStrong: there is currently no archive or museum in Galicia devoted to emigration that explains, in an educational way, how it came about
porque.quoteAfter: — a defining chapter of our recent history.

propuesta.proposal: To create the ESCOLA MUSEO DA EMIGRACIÓN, which will work to preserve and share the historical memory and the creations of successive generations of emigrants.
objectives: To promote and encourage activities aimed at establishing a documentation centre on emigration, building a broad database that can in turn support many kinds of research on emigration to the Americas in the 19th and 20th centuries.

To create a museum with a strong public-outreach role, presenting the values and contribution of Galician emigrants to the building and development of their host countries, and to the progress of Galicia itself through the founding of schools, foundations, charitable works, colleges, businesses and a long list of initiatives that drove development in the regions they had left.

viaje.title: The American adventure
viaje.lead: With a permanent section and a temporary one, the exhibition will use photographs, objects, documents and newspapers of the time to show the stages of the voyage to the Americas, the host countries and the different trades emigrants took up in each of them.

spaces.text: Emigrants' social centre, with a café, a meeting room and a place to gather. Running events and activities, and bringing together emigrants and anyone interested in the subject.

ruta.title: Guided walk through Gaxate
ruta.text: A guided walk through the village, with an audio guide, will tell visitors the story of its houses and families, bringing out everything distinctive and anecdotal about emigration and Gaxate's indianos, as well as the life of a Galician village in the first half of the 20th century.

art.hero: Illustration: a large steam ocean liner moored in port, with smoke rising from its funnels, gulls, a lighthouse on the coast, cranes and a crowd waving goodbye on the quay. In the foreground, an old suitcase covered in labels and a postcard dated 1913.
art.gaxate: Illustration: green, misty hills and the village of Gaxate, with white-galleried indiano houses among oak trees and a hórreo beside the path. In the foreground, a young man seen from behind with his suitcase, looking towards the horizon.
art.galiciaMap: Map of Galicia with a dot marking A Lama
art.escuela: Illustration: the Castro de Gaxate school, a low stone building with a tiled roof and large white windows, beside the woods. In front, villagers carry stones and timber to build it.
art.letterMap: Map: a letter travels along a dotted route from the Amazon, in South America, to Gaxate, in Galicia.
art.porque: Illustration: an archive table seen from above, with old photographs, letters, envelopes, stamps, a postcard, a bellows camera and a half-open trunk.
art.propuesta: Illustration: under a warm sky, the Castro school with a hanging sign that reads “Escola Museo da Emigración”. In front, the book “Galegos: As máns de América”, with a black cover and gold lettering, opens.
art.viaje: Illustration: the ocean liner crosses the sea from left to right while, behind it, we pass the Galician quay of farewell, night on the open sea, a warmly lit American port, a large emigrant hotel, the return through the fog and an indiano house with a white gallery and a palm tree.
art.coleccion: Illustration: a large old leather suitcase with brass fittings opens, and travel labels naming the materials to be exhibited fly out of it.
art.casaPlan: Illustrated plan of the house-museum: an irregular walled plot, with a slanted left wall and the road along the bottom. Reception and the entrance are at the bottom right. Exhibition panels run along the bottom wall and the slanted left wall. The route, marked with arrows, leaves the entrance towards the left, goes up the left side, crosses the top and comes down into the buildings. In the left building: at the top, the ground floor with the screening room and the book archive, and the upper floor with the documentary and sound archive; below that, the main temporary-exhibition hall; at the bottom, the toilets on the left and the shop and bookshop to their right. In the centre, the courtyard with a marquee. On the right, the tourist accommodation. Along the bottom row, the café.
art.rutaMap: Illustrated map of Gaxate: a dotted path runs through the village between meadows, oak trees and numbered indiano houses.
art.footerMap: Dotted route crossing the Atlantic from South America and ending in Gaxate
